children: The Ibovespa rose nearly 1.5% to trade around the 182,000 mark on Wednesday following the release of a new election poll.

A Quaest poll on voting intentions for president in the October election showed President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, viewed by markets as more fiscally restrictive amid elevated domestic yields and weak business activity, in a technical tie.
Lula had 42% of voting intentions in a potential runoff versus 41% for Flávio Bolsonaro.
Meanwhile, Brazilian bond yields declined after GDP data showed a sharp contraction in consumer spending.
Also, oil prices pulled back from recent peaks following a rally driven by escalating Middle East tensions, offering some relief to credit-sensitive stocks.
However, energy costs and yields remain elevated.
Major banks gained, with Banco do Brasil up nearly 1%.
Utilities also advanced, with Sabesp rising over 1% and Eneva adding more than 2%.
Petrobras fell 0.5% as oil prices declined.

title: Ibovespa Rises Following New Election Poll
